controls_results.method: deductive symbolic case analysis of the immutable snapshot

controls.attack: Check that four-deck isolation starts from an actual five-deck witness for every target.
controls.derivation: For the least residue r of x, r<m^5 and its five base-m digits a_i give the all-positive tuple (i,a_i,+1), whose encodings sum to [r+C]P=R.

controls.attack: At every dyadic level test both a true left query and a false left query, with sign labels allowed in either half.
controls.derivation: A true left predicate supplies a left witness. If it is false, no incoming witness uses the left half, so at least one uses the disjoint right half. The argument depends only on occurrence labels, not their sign ordering.

controls.attack: Recompute the exact restriction and full-scan counts without copying the producer's arithmetic.
Try to leave the residual W outside F_4 after all four labels have been isolated on an exact path.
controls.derivation: At singleton subsets the preserved witness has a fifth occurrence e_4 in unchanged F_4. Rearranging its five-sum equality gives encoding(e_4)=R-sum_{i=0}^3 encoding(e_i)=W, so the attempted counterexample contradicts the invariant.

controls.attack: Remove the mapping from a matching fifth-deck encoding to its occurrence coefficient label.
controls.derivation: Encoding equality identifies W but no longer supplies sigma_4 and d_4, so this labelled decoder cannot form its fifth scalar coefficient. The argument stops at W as required.

controls.attack: Check identity encodings and exact scalar size before the final reduction modulo N.
controls.derivation: For sufficiently large prime N, m<N and every nonzero labelled coefficient sigma(d+1)m^i is nonzero modulo N. Also m^5<32N and the absolute unreduced decoder integer is <3m^5<96N, requiring only O(log N) exact bits.

controls.attack: Allow multiple positive or negative F_4 labels to have the same encoding W and select any one.
controls.derivation: For matching coefficients c_4,c_4', [(c_4-c_4')]P=0. Since P has order N, c_4=c_4' modulo N, so all selected labels yield the same xhat modulo N and pass the same final equality.

controls.attack: Make an F_4 encoding collide with an encoding in a restricted deck.
controls.derivation: Every occurrence keeps its deck index in its label, and the residual scan ranges only over F_4 labels. An equal encoding from another deck cannot replace the fifth coefficient or erase the four isolated labels.

controls.attack: Inject an incorrect restriction reply and follow the selected branch.
controls.derivation: If the selected branch has no witness, no F_4 entry matches W. If another witness survives, recovery can still return a genuinely correct candidate. Thus corruption is never enough to create an incorrect accepted logarithm, although the producer's shorthand should include this witness-preserving third case.

controls.attack: Feed a nonmatching fifth label or an arithmetically corrupted candidate to the final gate.
controls.derivation: The gate accepts only when [xhat]P=Q. As P generates a group of prime order N, acceptance implies xhat=x modulo N; an incorrect candidate is rejected.
